cards.explanation: The answer is the Herodians. The text says the Pharisees sent their disciples to Jesus "…along with the Herodians." So the question comes from that group, not from the Pharisees themselves. Sending a whole delegation to ask one question is a plan with a lot of moving parts, friends.

The answer is False. The text says the opposite. They tell Jesus, "You seek favor from no one, because You pay no attention to external appearance." That's another compliment on the pile, friends. They keep stacking them higher and higher, like cookies on one plate.

The answer is taxes. They ask, "Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?" The text says the Pharisees conspired to trap Jesus in His words (Matthew 22:15). So this yes-or-no question comes straight out of that plan. Keep that in mind as the story goes on, friends.

The answer is hypocrites. Jesus says, "You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?" The text tells us He knew their evil intent. All those sweet words were sitting on top of something else. And He names it right away, with no wind-up.

The answer is the men testing Him, the same men who came to test Him. Jesus says, "Show Me the coin used for the tax." and the text says, "…they brought Him a denarius." So the men testing Him are the ones who bring the coin. I think it's funny that their test brings its own coin, but that's just me.

The answer is Caesar's! Jesus asks whose image and inscription are on the coin, and they answer, “Caesar’s.” Now the men who came with all the questions are the ones answering, and they're the ones who brought Him the coin (Matthew 22:19). That's like walking into a meeting to grill somebody and ending up presenting the slides. Their own answer sets up what Jesus says next.

The answer is False. What Jesus actually says is, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s." He never tells them not to pay. He answers the question with the coin they brought Him, and with one line about Caesar and God.

The answer is True. The text says, "…when they heard this, they were amazed." Then they left Him and went away. They came to trap Him in His words, and they walked away amazed instead. I'd be amazed too, friends. The story isn't over yet.
